what_happened: Research for the routing_agents_hard->hard_contracts migration found that lean's manifest declares a bare top-level 'contracts' context directory identical to core's, and the deployed .claude/context/contracts/{anti-analysis,reference-grounding,adversarial-verification}.md are confirmed byte-identical to lean's domain-specific override content, not core's generic content -- meaning every --hard dispatch of any task_type today silently reads lean-flavored H2/H3/H4 contracts due to a deploy-time directory clobber, independent of this task's named scope.

All four lean/cslib hard agents and core's anti-analysis.md 'Domain Specialization' section cite domain contract overrides at an extension-namespaced path (@.claude/extensions/lean/context/contracts/*.md) that does not exist anywhere in the deployed tree (.claude/extensions/<ext>/ deploys manifest.json only). check-extension-docs.sh Rule G, built to catch exactly this dangling-reference class, does not match this path shape due to its regex requiring the literal substring .claude/context/contracts/ immediately after .claude/.

Planning measured a blast radius well beyond the dispatch's 6 scope items: retiring the six -hard AGENTS forces retiring six orphaned hard SKILLS too (check-extension-docs Rule A fails on a skill dir absent from provides.skills and vice versa), and ~50 source-store files cite the twelve by name (lint-agent-contracts.sh has 6 hardcoded roster arrays that log_fail on a missing rostered file; collapsed-blocks/registry.tsv row 12 uses cslib-implementation-hard-agent.md as its exemplar; books/opencode-agents.json; four index-entries.json; ten core context/doc files cite a hard agent illustratively).

Dispatch scope item 5 says remove gate16 and its gate-registry.data row. Measured blocker the dispatch did not know: lint-gate-registry.sh Check E FAILS unless gate ids are contiguous from 1, and the registry holds 1..27 -- so removing id 16 forces renumbering gates 17-27 (40 refs in verify-deploy.sh plus 7 other files, plus gate-cache churn). gate16 already passes when zero manifests declare the keys, so the plan keeps gate16 in place as the absence-assertion guard the dispatch itself said to decide on separately, at zero renumbering cost.

The research report's per-domain -hard agent diff work made the gating question answerable without re-diffing; this pass only had to close the one question it left open (confirmed: standard lean-implementation-agent.md carries no phase_number, sorry_inventory, or Zero-Debt content, so that procedural residue needs a real destination rather than being droppable).
